defects.round_3_verification: Fix 5c0348f (fresh markers in their own bounded TtlSingleFlightCache `freshMarks`, max 2000, 3-min TTL; `flags` is no longer touched by lookups). Dev's converted test passes. Independent variant (shipQaRound3.spec.ts): 2 100 lookups alternated between two users (30/min cap then 429s) after a succeeded ship was composed, status cache invalidated, ship re-read: ship_succeeded still 1 and ship_stage_completed unchanged. Code review: the only writers of `flags` are markOnce (per ship x event x stage), cancel-requested and watchdog-cancelled; none is reachable by unknown-ID lookups. Residual observation (not a defect): `freshMarks` is itself a 2000-entry LRU, so a flood can evict another user's fresh marker, costing that user at most one extra counted lookup; memory stays bounded.
defects.title: Fresh-ID markers share the bounded `flags` LRU and are written even for refused requests: a user can flush other ships' cancel/watchdog/metric de-dup flags
defects.repro: `flags.set('fresh:<user>:<cid>')` runs BEFORE recordMiss, and `flags` (max 2000, LRU) also holds `cancel:`, `wdcancel:` and `metric:` de-dup keys. After the 30/min cap is reached every further distinct fresh ID still inserts a marker before the 429 is thrown, so ~2 100 requests flush the cache. Reproduced: a succeeded ship's metrics are emitted once; after a stranger floods 2 100 fresh IDs (30 x 200, rest 429) and the status cache is invalidated, `ship_succeeded` is emitted a SECOND time (duplicated metrics corrupt the success-rate dashboard; an evicted `cancel:` flag turns CANCELLED into SUPERSEDED once V-4 is on; an evicted `wdcancel:` flag lets the watchdog re-cancel)
defects.impact: Authenticated metric corruption / flag loss; memory stays bounded. Not exploitable for data access.
defects.suggested_fix: Keep the fresh markers in their own small Map/cache (max ~200, TTL 3 min) and/or set the marker only after recordMiss succeeded.

defects.round_3_verification: Fix 6bb6b88 (redactLine catches RangeError and returns the REPLACEMENT for that line only). Both converted tests pass. Independent probes: lines of 1/6/20 MB of the three throwing shapes (ghp_+letters, keyword+opening quote, eyJ- run) with a secret before AND after in the same line, and an 8 MB line between ordinary lines: no throw, the secret never survives, the neighbouring lines stay readable and are still redacted, the output is deterministic and idempotent; the logs route answers 200. Lines that do not overflow (e.g. 20 MB of letters or spaces with a secret at either end) are redacted in place, so nothing is skipped. Judgement of Dev's deviation 'an oversized line that overflows the regex stack is replaced whole': ACCEPTABLE. It is fail-closed, loses at most one pathological line (a legitimate build line of >5 MB is not realistic; the 5 MB log view cap already truncates), does not shift any other line, and offsets stay safe (getLogs clamps offset to the redacted text length). Residual observation: a still-growing un-newlined line that crosses the overflow threshold changes from partly redacted text to the replacement between two polls; the client's offset is clamped, so it cannot error.
defects.title: A single log line of ~6 MB or more makes redactText throw RangeError; the logs route answers 503 for everyone
defects.repro: String.replace overflows V8's regexp backtrack stack on one un-newlined line: `ghp_` + 8 MB of letters, `<keyword>="` + 8 MB, and `eyJ-` x 2 M all throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` (threshold ~5-6 MB for the GitHub-token/JWT patterns, ~8 MB for the widened quoted pattern; 4 MB is fine). The reviewed baseline already threw for the GitHub-token pattern; the quoted pattern is newly affected by the widening. Through the route the response is 503 (fail-closed: no secret and no stack text in the body, verified), but the whole stage log is unreadable and downloadable for the starter and platform members

defects.repro: Real JSON.stringify chain of `{"before":"b4","<password-key>":"alphaW \"betaW\" gammaW deltaW"}` (or `alphaW\" betaW gammaW deltaW`): level 1 redacts the whole value; at level 2 the embedded quote is serialised with 3 backslashes (delimiter: 1), at level 3 with 7 (delimiter: 3). deviations_review_round_3.ref: cache-composed metrics (ship_succeeded, ship_stage_completed, ship_failed) carry only the ship correlation id, not the request id
deviations_review_round_3.reason: They are emitted once per ship at compose time (shared across requests by the single-flight cache), so no single request id is correct; the ship id is the join key. Request-scoped lines (ship_authz_denied, ship_rate_limited, cancel/retry/watchdog logs) do carry requestId.

deviations_review.ref: NEW: redaction widened beyond the §7.3 text (optional bounded _SUFFIX after the keyword, optional quote before the separator, quoted value taken whole)
deviations_review.reason: Needed to cover env-var echoes (QA-001) and JSON (QA-003); QA found it a superset of the spec-literal pattern on a 6 000-line differential fuzz with no loss, and benign build output is untouched (29 lines). Known, harmless over-redaction: hyphenated forms such as `token-based: yes`. Gaps remain at the edges of the new grammar: QA-010 (escaped quotes), QA-011 (glued tail). Recommend the Architect records the widened grammar in the §7.3 spec delta together with the fixes for those two.

deviations_review.ref: NEW: dedupe key = user + all nine validated input fields
deviations_review.reason: Exactly what DD-14/BT-24 need: verified field by field and for genuinely identical POSTs. Defaults are applied before keying, so omitted vs explicit defaults still dedupe.

deviations_review.ref: NEW: JWT match starts only at the beginning of a base64url run (lookbehind)
deviations_review.reason: Removes the quadratic behaviour (QA-002) and redacts JWTs after space, = : ( " . , / Bearer and ANSI colour codes (11 placements tested). Narrowing vs the original `\b`: a JWT glued directly after a hyphen (`x-eyJ...`) is no longer matched by the JWT pattern itself (still caught when a keyword/Authorization header precedes it). Observation, not raised as a defect.
